newsitem.title: UK: Finer tops prices sheared in Bradford wool market.
newsitem.headline: Finer tops prices sheared in Bradford wool market.

text.p: Most tops prices were down in the Bradford market as confidence was punctured by sharp declines in prices for merinos in Australia and New Zealand, trade sources reported on Thursday.
Finer tops from 66s to 58s blended lost 12-15 pence per kg with 70s Super quoted at 505 pence, 20 pence down in the week.
Among the coarser values, 50s-58s English fared best ending unchanged.
Price testing by sellers - some of whom who cut their already low asking bids by up to five percent - contributed to the general gloom when no buyers were found, brokers said.
There were no reports of new business and sellers continued to subsist on repeat orders, they added.

Several sources, including retail buyers, were sceptical that earlier signs of recovery would resume or that hopes of significant price rises by the end of the year on the back of fine merino values would be realised.

"But those (topmakers) looking on the bright side still say that deliveries are going out well and orderbooks are sound enough to prevent any immediate anxiety" despite the recent volatility, one source said.
